failure_summary.description: Both trajectories added unnecessary code beyond the needed tool calls; one also redefined tool-related models and failed at runtime.
One trajectory repeated dates and party size as filter arguments even though those constraints were already reflected in cached results.
One trajectory changed the capitalization of a user-provided flight-class value.

patch.reasoning: The skill is empty, and the batch shows that follow-up planning should use existing cached results with only newly added constraints, while generated code should remain minimal and runnable. Preserving user-provided value spelling also prevents avoidable parameter mismatches.

edits.content:
## Learned rules
- For follow-up requests, use relevant cached results and apply only newly stated constraints. Do not repeat itinerary details already reflected in those results or recalculate their dates; perform a new search only when the cache is missing or no longer applicable.
- Keep generated code to the necessary tool calls and cache operations. Tool functions and models are already provided: do not import or redefine them, add unrelated calculations or output formatting, or claim no planning is needed when a new constraint must be applied.
- Preserve the spelling and capitalization of values taken from the conversation when passing them to tools; do not title-case or otherwise normalize them.
